https://jerseyeveningpost.com/news/2026/.text: A MAN on a mission to visit every parliament he can has declared Jersey’s States Assembly the best he has experienced so far… after touring 32 legislatures across Europe and beyond in around just 18 months. UK-based university learning technology technologist and TV quizzer Nicholas Elliott has turned an unlikely passion into an international pursuit, travelling to more than 50 countries and contacting parliaments one by one in the hope they will open their doors to him. Jersey became his 32nd parliament last month – and, he says, left the biggest impression to date. “I’m going to say this: they’re the best, the best I’ve ever been to,” he said in a Bailiwick Podcasts interview. Mr Elliott’s fascination with parliaments began around just two years ago, following what he initially assumed would be a fairly mundane tour of Westminster with his visiting Polish mother-in-law and daughter. “I thought to myself, ‘This is not going to be very interesting’,” he admitted, but explained that it was not long before he found himself captivated by the history and traditions of the Palace of Westminster. “I started learning things about a country which I’ve lived in all my life… I was so amazed by the rich history the UK has. That’s how it basically started. I got the bug from that moment onwards.” Since then, Mr Elliott has written to legislatures across Europe and further afield asking whether they would host him, comparing himself to a “mystery shopper” for democracy. “I’m just a normal person. I’m not a politician, I’m not an academic, I’m not a journalist,” he said, “But when I arrive, sometimes [parliamentary staff] think I’m a celebrity… They’re always asking, ‘Why do you want to visit our parliament?'” The answer, he says, is all about truly knowing how the people and institutions that shape citizens’ way of life operate, and being better able to hold them to account. Comparing elected politicians to tenants looking after a rented property on behalf of voters, Mr Elliott explained: “People vote for politicians and then go, ‘My work here is done. Carry on for five years.’ “I think, wouldn’t you want to meet the person? Wouldn’t you want to know what they’re doing? When the ‘contract’ comes to an end, I want to decide whether I want to keep you as my tenant or whether I want somebody better.” He believes ordinary people should take a greater interest in how their legislatures operate and says some of his visits have even prompted parliaments to rethink how accessible they are. “Some of them have actually set up tours afterwards. They’ve listened to my advice and made them available for schoolchildren or the general public. That’s transparency. Civic engagement is what I’m all about.” The Parliament of Hungary Not every parliament has been so welcoming, however. “There are countries which are, bluntly, not democratic,” he said. “Those are the countries who basically say, ‘No one can visit our parliament’ – even people who live there.” As for Jersey, Mr Elliott said the visit also transformed his understanding and appreciation of the Island. Like many people in Britain, he had assumed Jersey was simply part of the UK before discovering its unique constitutional relationship with the Crown, its own parliament, immigration rules and legal system – a revelation he likened to discovering that “a dolphin isn’t actually a fish”. He said he particularly enjoyed learning about William the Conqueror’s connection, King John’s loss of Normandy, the German Occupation and the role of the Bailiff during the Second World War. Inside the States Building, he was fascinated by the architecture, how the courtroom directly adjoins the Assembly chamber, and the Bailiff’s ceremonial mace. Mr Elliott in the Parliament of Canada Mr Elliott – who has been a contestant on numerous gameshows – also praised the member of the States Greffe who guided his visit, saying she answered every question he could throw at her. “I was trying to catch her out because I know my stuff,” he laughed. “Every question I asked, she knew the answer.” But more so, he was impressed by how “direct” Jersey’s political system felt. While Islanders may have their own gripes with representation, Mr Elliott said the proximity to local decision-makers was an asset he felt more people should appreciate, particularly given how challenging it can be to contact and exchange views with MPs in the UK. As a result, Mr Elliott said Jersey should be on every politics student’s itinerary. Mr Elliott in the Slovenian parliament “If you really want to see another [country’s parliament], go to Jersey,” he said. “You have a beautiful history that goes back more than 1,000 years, and you can see how a small Assembly can actually work. It shows you what pure democracy looks like.” His parliamentary world tour continued this month with Jamaica, where, he joked, he would have to swap shorts for a jacket despite the warm weather because of the chamber’s strict dress code. Ahead of that trip, however, he said that Jersey was proudly at the top of his parliamentary league table, even joking that, if someone could “put in a good word” to help him move to the Island, he might one day stand for election himself. https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Lily Hooper left her home in Sydney’s south-west about 8am on 12 August, after telling family she was going for a hike in the Nattai national park. Photograph: NSW Police View image in fullscreen Lily Hooper left her home in Sydney’s south-west about 8am on 12 August, after telling family she was going for a hike in the Nattai national park. Photograph: NSW Police New South Wales Fears for missing Sydney teen who hasn’t been seen since leaving for hike on Wednesday Fresh search teams to scour Nattai national park for Lily Hooper, 18, who failed to return home from a bushwalk Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Lisa Cox and AAP Fri 14 Aug 2026 21.07 EDT Last modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 21.18 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The search for an 18-year-old bushwalker missing in the Southern Highlands of New South Wales since Wednesday is continuing, with fresh teams arriving at the Nattai national park on Saturday morning. Lily Hooper left her home in Sydney’s south-west about 8am on 12 August, after telling family she was going for a hike in the national park, north-west of Mittagong. The experienced hiker was reported missing when she did not return that evening and could not be reached, despite having sent messages from the park earlier in the day. A search began with her car found parked on Wanganderry Road, near the start of the Bonnum Pic Walking Trail at High Range, about 11pm that night. On Saturday, NSW police said in a statement that initial inquiries indicated Hooper reached the summit of Bonnum Pic about mid-morning on Wednesday, but had made no further contact since then. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email A multi-agency search – involving local police, regional Police Rescue, NSW Ambulance, Fire and Rescue NSW, the State Emergency Service and members of Hooper’s family – has not found any further signs of the teen. Defence force personnel joined the search on Friday, with drones, an ambulance helicopter and specialist rescuers, including trail-bike riders, also involved. A NSW police spokesperson said the search continued overnight and fresh teams arrived at the park at 7am on Saturday. On Friday, Det Insp Benjamin Bowles said authorities were concerned for Hooper’s safety. But he said he remained optimistic, and that Hooper was an experienced hiker. “We have not been able to fully confirm what supplies [Hooper] had with her at the time, but we are still hopeful that we will be able to locate her safe and sound,” he said. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion “We don’t have any information to suggest that this is anything other than an overdue hiker.” The NSW premier, Chris Minns, told reporters on Friday he was “praying for good news”. “Our heart goes out to that young walker’s family,” he said. “We know this must be heartbreaking and incredibly anxious.” Hooper is described as Caucasian in appearance, about 175cm tall, slim, and with long blond hair and blue eyes. She was last seen wearing a shirt and shorts, but police said it was not known what clothing or supplies she took for the hike. Police said anyone who may have seen Hooper, had information about her whereabouts or who walked the Bonnum Pic walking trail on Wednesday, should contact Moss Vale police station on 02 4869 7899 or Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000. https://www.irishmirror.ie/daniel-kinaha.text: Mob boss Daniel Kinahan is now on his way back to Ireland aboard the government jet. Kinahan (49) was picked up in Dubai this morning after gardai flew on the Irish Air Corps €53 million Dassault Falcon 6X to the United Arab Emirates city on Saturday. The flight touched down in Dubai on Saturday night , and the handover took place today. The jet took off from Dubai's Al Maktoum International Airport at 1:19pm Dubai time (10:19am Irish time). It is expected to land in Dublin's Baldonnel Airport at around 7:20pm tonight - and he will be taken straight to the Special Criminal Court . This is the first time the government jet, purchased last year, will be used to transport an alleged criminal to this country. The jet, which has a call sign of ‘Irl290,’ is typically used to ferry the Taoiseach and government ministers around the globe. It has, however, also been used to transport members of the Ranger Wing to and from locations, as well as to pick up people in emergency situations. In past similar operations an Irish Air Corps Airbus C295 was used to pick up Gerry ‘The Monk’ Hutch and Sean McGovern. However, the government jet is far more efficient because it can quickly make the journey from Dubai without any stops. A source said: “This is ultimately about getting Kinahan to Ireland as quickly and as securely as possible - both for him and the Gardaí with him.” This weekend’s security operation is set to involve the Defence Forces, Irish Prison Service and multiple Garda units, including the Armed Support Unit, Emergency Response Unit, National Drugs and Organised Crime Bureau, and Garda Air Support. Several road closures are also expected as Gardaí are hopeful of moving Kinahan straight to the Special Criminal Court without delay. Once back on Irish soil Kinahan will be arrested on the tarmac in relation to directing a criminal organisation. He can be charged once he enters the confines of the court. It is understood the charge encompasses a number of murder plots carried out over the course of the Kinahan Hutch feud - which first erupted in September 2015. While the exact details of the security operation are being kept under wraps, sources say Kinahan will be immediately brought from Baldonnel to Dublin’s Criminal Courts of Justice in Parkgate Street under a heavy armed escort. As with his right-hand man Sean McGovern, Kinahan may be driven out of the military airport in an unmarked Garda car, while ‘decoy’ vehicles could also be used. If this approach occurs, it will be followed in the front and back by several other unmarked vehicles carrying armed Gardaí. However sources say it is also possible that another extraordinary step could be taken in light of the security concerns surrounding the operation. Sources say Kinahan could potentially be flown out of Baldonnell via helicopter to another location, where he may then be more speedily transported to the Special Criminal Court. Special arrangements have been made to open the courts' doors in Parkgate Street for a hearing on Sunday night. Three judges of the Special Criminal Court will be in place as Kinahan is escorted under armed guard from the building's basement, where he will have been driven in just moments before. The court will then hear evidence of Kinahan’s arrest, charge and caution from a senior Garda. Kinahan is entitled to legal representation and to be present in court for the brief hearing. It is then expected that he will be remanded into custody, and Gardaí will hand him over to the Irish Prison Service. Kinahan will likely be brought back down into the basement of the courts building, where he will enter a newly purchased prison van. The Irish Prison Service recently purchased the bullet-and-bomb-proof van from the UK to carry the likes of Kinahan and other high profile prisoners in the future. Gardai will escort the van to Portlaoise Prison in Co Laois, the country’s maximum security prison. Documents will then be signed to transfer Kinahan to the prison as a remand prisoner. He will then be housed on the ‘A’ Block of the prison, which is deemed the most secure section. The ‘A’ is also home to Sean McGovern, who was recently jailed for 24 years for his role in directing a criminal organisation in relation to the murder of innocent Dad Noel ‘Duck Egg’ Kirwan and in relation to the surveillance and targeting of Hutch associate James ‘Mago’ Gately. Sources say Kinahan is however likely to be held in isolation for the duration of his remand. It is also envisaged that his future court hearings before a trial would be held via video link. A trial is not expected to take place until at least a year from now - with sources previously stating that the file in the case is extremely large. Prison authorities have also stepped up security measures in Portlaoise - with Kinahan likely to be kept on ‘suicide watch’ for a period of time. The case against Daniel Kinahan is understood to allege that he directed the Kinahan organisation during the course of the murderous feud that saw 18 people killed. It is understood to specifically allege that Kinahan directed the criminal gang in the attempt to murder Hutch associate ‘Mago’ from October 2015 into mid 2017. It is also understood to relate to a plot to murder ‘The Monk’ himself in Lanzarote in December 2015. Some of the allegations against Kinahan are believed to rely on encrypted conversations uncovered from the seizure of several phones from the cartel. The so-called ‘Pretty Good Privacy’ (PGP) devices contain conversations between someone who will be alleged to be Kinahan - and Sean McGovern - as well as other associates. McGovern, who was Kinahan’s closest confidant, was nailed in part by encrypted conversations intercepted by gardai that showed how he and other cartel members plotted the murder of Mr Kirwan and set about targeting Gately. Gardai are understood to allege that encrypted handles known as ‘Bon Neww,’ 'Bon4' and 'Cap' which communicated with and gave orders to McGovern and others at the height of the feud, belonged to Daniel Kinahan. In one conversation revealed during McGovern’s case, the Special Criminal Court heard how Sean McGovern told 'Cap' following the Regency Hotel shooting: “Mate I’m fuming I swear to God what about doing Mink’s daughter or will that bring too much heat?” ‘Cap’ then responded, “Yes, but maybe only Neddie,” in a message referencing Eddie Hutch, a brother of Gerry ‘The Monk’ Hutch. Those messages were sent on February 7th, 2017, just one day before Eddie was ultimately murdered by the cartel at his home in Poplar Row in Dublin. Other encrypted chats revealed that the cartel plot to track James Gately was first hatched in October 2015 and later in 2017 ‘Bon Neww’ directed McGovern to go after him. “Hate the horrible rat bag. Get Mago,” Bon Neww (allegedly Kinahan) told McGovern in April 2017. On April 3, 2017, Estonian hitman Imre Arakas flew into Ireland and the following day was arrested by gardai at an address at Blakestown Cottages. Officers ultimately seized a Blackberry device containing the encrypted instructions he was receiving from the handle they suspect was Kinahan. The court heard how a member of the Garda Emergency Response Unit took photos of the conversations before they were remotely wiped. In those messages Arakas was conversing with ‘Bon Neww’ about using a ‘silencer’ and shooting Gately in the head from a distance. The court also heard that ‘Bon Neww’ relayed messages to Arakas, including informing him that Gately ‘drives most days, he seems to go to Newry and back.’ Arakas was also told to Google a picture of Gately, with the message informing him that the second image on the site was a clear picture of him.
